name: Ridgepost Capital, Inc.
reason: Acquisition-built private-markets manager (acquisitions 1.34x 10y FCF, shares up 22%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 3.9x) with GAAP EPS of 0.17 at 0.46x its 10y peak and fundraising tied to capital-markets activity.

name: Perimeter Solutions, Inc.
reason: Near-monopoly fire-retardant supplier, but earnings swing with wildfire seasons and a dominant US Forest Service customer, and GAAP EBIT margin ranged from 42% to -31% in three years.

name: TPG, Inc.
reason: Alternative asset manager whose earnings depend on fundraising and realizations driven by capital markets; GAAP EPS went from 28.61 (2021) to 0.45 (2025) with a 171% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap.

name: Brookfield Business Corp.
reason: Leveraged holding vehicle for private-equity-style businesses with net debt/EBITDA 6.6x, GAAP losses in 2023-25 and a 5.1% EBIT margin; it has no franchise economics and cannot be forecast.

name: ESAB Corp.
reason: Solid welding consumables franchise, but the EBIT margin of 17.3% is at its 10y high in a cyclical industrial end market, with 8.7% average ROIC and a GAAP EPS dip in 2025 (-14.6%).

name: Corebridge Financial, Inc.
reason: Spread-based annuity and life insurer whose earnings depend on interest rates and credit spreads; GAAP EPS swung from 12.59 (2022) to -0.68 (2025).

name: F&G Annuities & Life, Inc.
reason: Fixed-indexed annuity spread lender dependent on rates and private credit; GAAP EPS ranges from 8.24 to -0.47 and consensus FY1 is -20%.

name: Adeia, Inc.
reason: Patent-licensing model whose revenue depends on lumpy renewals and litigation outcomes (EBIT margin -23% to 65% in 10y) and faces streaming/pay-TV disintermediation of its licensee base; adjusted EPS CAGR is only 4.6%.

name: Skyward Specialty Insurance Group, Inc.
reason: Fast-growing specialty P&C underwriter with EPS at a 1.0x peak (4.07 in 2025 vs 0.30 in 2021), but its underwriting record as a public company spans only about 4 years and is untested through a soft market.

name: BKV Corp.
reason: Natural gas producer whose earnings are set by gas prices (EBIT margin 56% to -17%), with net debt/EBITDA 6.0x and acquisitions at 14x FCF.

name: Atmus Filtration Technologies, Inc.
reason: Razor-blade-like filtration aftermarket with 28% average ROIC, net debt/EBITDA of only 1.2x, no acquisition-led growth and steady EPS (1.71 to 2.50 over 2020-25); FY2-3 consensus is 11-13%, but the 16.4% margin is at its high and long-run truck electrification needs testing.

name: Light & Wonder, Inc.
reason: Slot and iGaming content supplier with improving margins (27.2% at 10y high), but net debt/EBITDA is 3.8x, acquisitions and buybacks each absorb about 1x FCF, the history is volatile and IP litigation is outstanding.

name: Diebold Nixdorf, Inc.
reason: Post-bankruptcy ATM/retail hardware maker with a 4.0% average EBIT margin, negative average ROIC and secular decline in cash usage; this is a cheap but ordinary business.

name: AngloGold Ashanti Plc
reason: Gold miner with adjusted EPS at 1.0x its 10y max and EBIT margin 44.4% at a record (10y avg 20.6%); the gold price sets earnings.

name: NCR Atleos Corp.
reason: Recently spun ATM operator facing secular decline in cash use, with net debt/EBITDA 3.0x, only 4 years of history and a 146% adjusted-vs-GAAP EPS gap; this is a bargain without specialness.

name: Mach Natural Resources LP
reason: Oil and gas E&P with EBIT margin falling from 58.7% to 23.2% as commodity prices moved; earnings are unforecastable and FCF conversion is negative.

name: Slide Insurance Holdings, Inc.
reason: Florida homeowners insurer founded in 2021 with EPS at a 1.0x peak after a benign storm period; hurricane catastrophe and reinsurance-cost exposure make earnings binary.

name: The Cooper Cos., Inc.
reason: Member of the four-player contact lens oligopoly with secular myopia-management and daily-lens drivers; adjusted EPS grew 8.3%/yr over 10y with flat share count, and the margin is only at its 36th percentile, but the slowing CooperSurgical fertility business and acquisitions near 1x FCF need checking.

name: Solventum Corp.
reason: Recent 3M healthcare spin-off still separating ERP/supply chains and divesting P&F, with GAAP EBIT margin down to 8.6% from 23%, net debt/EBITDA 3.6x and inherited PFAS/litigation exposure.

name: Cirrus Aircraft Ltd.
reason: Leading personal-aircraft brand with net cash and 18.8% ROIC, but demand for luxury piston aircraft and jets is discretionary and cyclical, and EPS sits at a 1.0x peak with margins near their high.
